subject: research/simdesign-gaugescatter
professional: a senior FE / structural-optimisation analyst (stress-constrained sizing of sheet-metal parts); first checks: does the FE stress agree with a hand beam calculation, is the stress constraint mesh-converged before an optimiser is allowed to sit on it, and is the 'narrow feasible region' a property of the design or of the discretisation

evidence.correctness: Ran /tmp/claude-0/audit-gaugescatter/check.py (python3.13, scikit-fem 12.0.2, scipy 1.18.1). Mass: shipped mass_g equals the hand area w(L+H-w)+r^2(1-pi/4) times b times 7.85e-3 for four designs (e.g. w=14.7, r=9.8, b=2: 33.857 g both). Tip deflection: FE 0.421 mm for w=14.7 b=2 lies between Euler-Bernoulli frame bounds with centreline lengths (0.483) and rigid-corner lengths (0.351): pass. Stress: fails. For the DE gauge-2 design that sets the headline 33.32 g (seed 2, w=14.407, r=10.740), hand bending plus axial stress in the vertical arm 6F(L-w/2)/(b w^2)+F/(w b) = 108.7 MPa, above the 100 MPa limit, yet the h=2.5 search mesh reads 100.0 and marks it feasible; at h=0.5 the same solver reads 131.1. Beam theory alone needs w >= ~14.9 mm at b=2, so every lower-group (33.3-34.0 g) result is infeasible by hand calculation and the upper group (w~15.3-15.6, nominal 92-96 MPa) reads 112-118 MPa at h=0.5. The README's own arithmetic reproduces (price sd 0.0676 with seed 0, 0.0040 without; 41.01/35.57 = 1.153; seed-0 rules sub-search reproduced as infeasible, w=2.969 just under w_min 3), so the numbers are faithfully reported, but the feasibility they rest on is a coarse-mesh under-read.
evidence.completeness: Checked each claimed deliverable: 8 tests (README says 8; 8 pass), experiments/run.py and miss_rate.py with committed results.txt/json and miss_rate.txt/json whose numbers match every README bullet (13/900 feasible at 2 mm, 405-637 at 3-8 mm for rules, prices 1.10/1.55/1.98 at 8/10/12 mm, gap mean -1.85 g over n=79, 1 of 20 rules misses, bimodal 10+9 and 10+10). The seed-0 miss re-run directly reproduced. Live page https://marisstella.app/research/simdesign-gaugescatter/ returns 200. Did not re-run the 10-minute run.py in full. No stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: `cd research/simdesign-gaugescatter && python3.13 -m pytest -q tests`: 8 passed in 9.4 s. Five seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: plane-stress lambda replaced by the plane-strain lambda SURVIVED; tip load scaled by 0.8 SURVIVED; stress limit x1.15 caught; shear stress doubled in von Mises caught; laser web rule halved caught. No test compares the FE against an analytic solution (beam stress or deflection), so errors in constitutive law and load magnitude go unseen; test_gauge2_rules_subsearch_finds_a_feasible_design asserts the very coarse-mesh artefact the follow-up disproved.
evidence.craft: Read model.py, dfm.py, optimise.py, measures.py, tests, run.py, miss_rate.py. The whole engine (model, dfm, optimise, measures, export, stl) is a verbatim copy shared with at least nine sibling simdesign-gauge* projects (git show --stat 3ce926261), so a solver fix must be made in ten places. Dead code in solve(): model.py:105 (`... if False else None`) and model.py:107 (unused `fb`). pyproject.toml:8 description is copied from simdesign-patchsearch ('Does a patch-averaged stress measure change...'), not this project. export.py and stl.py are unused here. Experiment scripts are tidy and reproducible (fixed seeds, Pool(4)).
evidence.claims: Backed by files: every numeric README bullet matches results.txt / miss_rate.txt; AI-assistance and 'simulated only' statements on README and the served page; limitations name the untested mesh dependence. Not backed / stale: the README and live page still present 'The 2 mm gauge has a narrow feasible region' and 'Feasible results at 2 mm are bimodal' as findings and 'the cause of the two mass groups is unknown', while research/simdesign-gaugemesh (README lines 22-27) has since shown none of the 39 gauge-2 designs stays feasible on a finer mesh, i.e. the region is a mesh artefact; the subject carries no pointer to that result. 'The rules' real mass price is set by the web rule at thick gauges' is mesh-conditional and is not qualified.
evidence.fitness: A researcher could and did build on it: gaugemesh, gaugepatch, gaugefine, gaugebasins, gaugerestart, gaugebudget all cite it, mostly to undo it. As a standalone result the diagnosis 'seed 0 missed a narrow feasible region' is internally correct but explains an artefact of the h=2.5 mesh. Nearest prior work: stress-constrained structural optimisation, where mesh-dependence of the stress constraint is a known issue (Duysinx and Bendsoe 1998, IJNME 43:1453; Le et al. 2010, SMO 41:605), and penalty-based constraint handling in evolutionary search missing small feasible regions (Deb 2000, CMAME 186:311; Mezura-Montes and Coello 2011 survey). The finding is not new and, given the mesh result, not sound as a statement about the design.
evidence.domain: Against standard FE practice (a mesh-convergence check of the governing stress, and a hand-calculation sanity check, before using it as a design constraint; e.g. NAFEMS 'How to' guidance): neither was done. The governing stress is the maximum element-centroid von Mises value on a ~2.5 mm P2 mesh across a 14 mm arm, which sits ~1 mm inside the surface and under-reads by 12-31% here; the optimiser then rides exactly on that under-read (all feasible results at 97-100 MPa). A senior analyst would reject the stress constraint in the first hour: a one-line beam formula shows the 'best' design is over the limit.

defects.what: The stress constraint is the element-centroid peak on an unconverged h=2.5 mm mesh; every 'feasible' gauge-2 design sits at 97-100 MPa there but reads 112-131 MPa at h=0.5, and the headline 33.32 g design is over the 100 MPa limit by hand beam theory (108.7 MPa). The project's central objects (narrow 2 mm region, bimodal mass groups, gauge-2 winner) are discretisation artefacts

verdict: Below the bar. The bookkeeping is faithful: masses match the hand area formula, tip deflection sits inside Euler-Bernoulli frame bounds, every README number matches the committed outputs, the seed-0 miss reproduces, and 8 tests pass. But the stress the whole study turns on is a coarse-mesh under-read: the headline 33.32 g gauge-2 design is over the 100 MPa limit by a one-line beam formula (108.7 MPa) and reads 131 MPa at h=0.5, so the 'narrow feasible region' and the 'bimodal' groups the project diagnoses are artefacts of h=2.5, as the later simdesign-gaugemesh project in this repo confirmed; the README and live page do not say so. Two of five seeded solver mutants survive because no test compares against an analytic result. Correctness, claims and verification are each 2.
